A '''number sequence''' is a [[sequence]] of [[number]]s.

== Formal definition ==

Let $\mathbb{F}$ be a [[field (mathematical concept)|field]].

Any function

$$
A:\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{F}
$$

is a number sequence in $\mathbb{F}$.

== Description ==

The $n^{th}$ term of a sequence is often denoted by $a_n$. The sequence is then denoted by $(a_n)$.

=== Direct definition ===

The terms of certain number sequences can be described by a direct formula:

$$
a_n=f(n)
$$

where $f(n)$ is a well-defined function.

{{Hidden example}}

$$
a_n=\frac{1}{n}\\
\Rightarrow (a_n)_{n \ge 1}=1,\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{3},\cdots
$$
{{End hidden}}

=== Recursive definition ===

The terms of some number sequences can only be described recursively relative to previous terms:

$$
a_n=f(a_{n-1},a_{n-2},\cdots)
$$

== Classification ==

Number sequences are often described by the evolution of their terms as $n$ grows.

{| class="wikitable"
|-
! Name
! Characteristic
|-
| Constant
| $a_n = a_{n+1} \quad \forall n \in \mathbb{N}$
|-
| Increasing
| $a_n < a_{n+1} \quad \forall n \in \mathbb{N}$
|-
| Decreasing
| $a_n > a_{n+1} \quad \forall n \in \mathbb{N}$
|-
| Non-decreasing
| $a_n \le a_{n+1} \quad \forall n \in \mathbb{N}$
|-
| Non-increasing
| $a_n \ge a_{n+1} \quad \forall n \in \mathbb{N}$
|-
| Convergent
| $\lim_{n \to +\infty} a_n = \ell$
|-
| Bounded
| | $|a_n| \leq M \quad \forall n \in \mathbb{N}$
|-
| Upper-bounded
| $a_n \leq M \quad \forall n \in \mathbb{N}$
|-
| Lower-bounded
| $a_n \geq M \quad \forall n \in \mathbb{N}$
|}

== Behaviour ==

=== Convergence of $(a_n)$ ===

As discussed in [[#Classification]], 

$$
\lim_{n \to +\infty} a_n = \ell \iff (a_n) \text{ converges to } \ell
$$

In addition,

$$
\lim_{n \to +\infty} a_n = \ell \iff \limsup_{n \to \infty} a_n = \ell = \liminf_{n \to \infty} a_n
$$

by the definition of the [[Limit (mathematical concept)|limit]].

<ref>{{#cite:Q2447}}</ref>
